newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek finmin expects mkts to welcome 3-yr bond.
newsitem.headline: Greek finmin expects mkts to welcome 3-yr bond.

text.p: Greek Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said he expected the markets to give a warm welcome to Greece's first-ever three-year fixed coupon bond on Friday and added he planned a more active public debt management.

"We expect the market to extend a cordial welcome to the three-year fixed coupon bond to be auctioned on Friday," said Christodoulakis. "It is the finance ministry's first important step and should not be affected by external events."

He was apparently referring to a tax on interest income from interbank transactions that was initially presented by the government as a withhholding tax on interest on separate interbank deals and brought interbank trading to a halt on Tuesday.

"It is unfortunate that this incident occured. It will be excessive if investors submit lower bids on Friday because of this. It will show that the market reaction time is short on bad news and long on good news," he said.
Greece is going to auction 100 billion drachmas worth of three-year 11 percent coupon bonds on Friday along with 200 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs.
Christodoulakis said he wanted to ensure the market that the tax status of auctioned securities will always be clarified before the auctions.
No abrupt changes in rules will take place and the enrichment of investor portfolios with new debt instruments will be a priority, he said.

"We are against retroactive taxation," said Christodoulakis who pointed out that there will be no retroactive taxation on outstanding FRNs. "The refixing of outstanding FRNs will be based on the gross 12-month T-bill yield after January 1."
He declined to say how the ministry planned to implement the tax on new FRNs, pointing out that the matter was under study.
Greece will impose a 7.5 percent tax on T-bills and bonds that goes into effect on January 1.
Asked if he planned any changes on commissions received by banks for buying into government securities, Christodoulakis said changes could take place after consultations with banks.
The deputy finance minister stressed that the treasury gave high priority to the active debt management of public debt which in turn required the introduction of new instruments and institutions.
"We will move gradually in the direction of active debt management introducing new instruments and institutions," said Christodoulakis.

"We're studying the introduction of three-, five- and seven-year fixed coupon bonds but there has to be a period of getting used to the new instruments, the new psychology and this warrants careful steps," he said.
Christodoulakis added that it was his intention to inform the market of the treasury's borrowing programme in advance so that investors have ample time to plan.

He said he expected interest rates to follow a mild downward course in 1997 based on declining inflation. The impact of new taxes on yields and the availability of new instruments will help portfolio diversification.
National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou said on Tuesday in revealing details of the 1997 budget that inflation will be at 4.5 percent at end-1997. -- Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
